overview: The named-sound packet is the one sound packet in this family that a major anticheat actively intercepts. NoCheatPlus ships SoundDistance, a ProtocolLib listener on PacketType.Play.Server.NAMED_SOUND_EFFECT that cancels wither, enderdragon and lightning sounds when the player is too far from the sound origin, which removes fake distant-boss audio and reduces client noise. The rest of the corpus is registration plumbing: Artemis maps the packet name to a wrapper interface, and Negativity lists it in its packet-type registry. Bukkit playSound calls in Hydro, TruthfulAC and SafeguardAC are anticheat GUI sounds, not S29 handling.

checks.name: SoundDistance (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: Cancel named sound packets for wither, enderdragon and lightning events when the player is beyond the configured audible radius of the sound origin.
checks.how_it_works: A ProtocolLib BaseAdapter registered at ListenerPriority.LOW on PacketType.Play.Server.NAMED_SOUND_EFFECT (S29). It maintains a hardcoded set of boss and weather sound names (pre-1.9 resource keys plus 1.9 and 1.21 enum names), matched against the packet's sound field via getStrings().read(0) on legacy servers or the Bukkit access matchSounds() on modern ones. For a match it computes the squared horizontal distance between the player and the packet's x8 fixed-point position and cancels the packet when that exceeds the configured soundDistanceSq limit, counting each cancel on the packet.sound.cancel counter.
checks.detects: Server-side sound spoofing where distant boss spawns or weather events are audible to players who should not hear them; the check doubles as client-noise reduction.
checks.variations: No other anticheat implements a sound-distance check. Artemis registers the packet family in its repository (PacketPlayServerSoundEffectNamed at SERVER_PLAY + 64, plus custom, entity and stop variants) and Negativity lists NAMED_SOUND_EFFECT in its PacketType registry, but neither reads sound payloads.

checks.name: Named sound wrapper registration (Artemis)
checks.purpose: Register the named sound effect packet in Artemis's packet repository so the abstraction layer can dispatch S29 to typed wrapper interfaces.
checks.how_it_works: PacketRepository maps SERVER_PLAY + 64 to PacketPlayServerSoundEffectNamed, a marker interface extending PacketServer. The packet generator's HardcodeMap associates the NMS name PacketPlayOutNamedSoundEffect with the same interface. The interface declares no fields or methods; Artemis only needs the packet to be recognized and routed.
checks.detects: Nothing. This is packet-library plumbing; no Artemis check consumes the sound name, position, volume or pitch.
checks.variations: Artemis registers the full S29 family: custom, entity, named and stop sound variants. Elikill58-Negativity maps NAMED_SOUND_EFFECT in its universal PacketType enum used by its packet listeners.
